name: Data Converter
description: Convert anything in one DBX workbench panel: 13 formats (JSON / YAML / XML / Properties / TOML / INI / .env / CSV / TSV / Query / Headers / Cookie / HTML) in any combination, JSONPath / jq queries with JSON Schema validation, eight escape tools (URL / Base64 / HTML / JSON / Unicode / Hex / SQL / Regex), batch text to SQL (IN / NOT IN / INSERT), .xlsx / .csv / .tsv to JSON, Image ⇄ Base64, and a Byte Converter (B/KB/MB/GB/TB/PB on both the 1000 and 1024 scales, exact ⇄ human readable, batch totals, plus hex dump / byte array / binary string). A Time Converter turns timestamps and dates into each other (local, T-separated, UTC, ISO 8601 and relative) one value per line, with foldable results and copies that carry results only. A Code Gen page turns a JSON sample or a CREATE TABLE into TypeScript / Go / Java / Python models, and a Chart page renders an ECharts option (or bare numbers) as a real chart, 700 x 400 by default with custom width and height, exported as PNG or SVG. Pure frontend, no backend, works offline.
releaseNotes: A new Time Converter page turns timestamps and dates into each other. Paste one value per line — 2020-01-01, 2020-01-01 00:00:00, 2020-01-01T00:00:00, 1577836800 or 1577836800000 — and every line is converted into the notations you enable. Five shortcut buttons — Now, Today start, Yesterday, Week start and Month start — append the matching moment as a new line in one click, truncated to the second. Seven toggles cover Unix seconds, Unix milliseconds, local time, local time with T, UTC, ISO 8601 and relative time; local and local-with-T are on by default, so the everyday 2020-01-01 00:00:00 <-> 2020-01-01T00:00:00 swap works out of the box. Results come as one card per line: the header folds it away, moving the caret to line N highlights card N, every value copies on click, and the Copy button writes results only — one output line per input line, fields joined by spaces, no index, no original value, no labels. Relative time stays for reading and never enters the copy. A batch caps at 2000 lines and a bad line is flagged on its own. All eleven pages are translated into 14 languages, and everything runs locally: no network, no eval.
